title: A tripartite genetic conflict system controls hybrid sterility in rice.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the only public artifact tied to this paper: Zenodo record 20586867 ('Code for: A tripartite genetic conflict system...') holding one 16,864-byte zip, and its GitHub source tree (18 entries, all .py/.sh/README/LICENSE/environment.yml, zero data files). Read the repo README, which states 'This repository contains code only.' Confirmed Europe PMC has no full text and no supplementary files (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N). NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42658938 returned no GEO, SRA, BioProject or BioSample link, only a subscription full-text link. Searched NCBI BioProject and GEO for RHS3 and for Oryza glaberrima sterility: 0 hits. Dryad search: 0 hits. The Science article page and its supplementary PDF both return HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything biological: that RHS3 is a major quantitative trait locus (a genome region whose variants shift a measured trait), that it encodes three genes named MAO (toxin), DUN and JIA (antidotes), the autophagy-based detoxification mechanism, and the inferred de novo origin in the AA-genome rice lineage. All of this comes from the abstract alone; I could not read the methods, the figures or any supplementary table.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No data is downloadable. The Zenodo/GitHub deposit is 16.8 KB of analysis scripts with no input or output tables; its README says explicitly 'This repository contains code only' and points to 'accessions in the paper and supplement'. The paper and its supplement are behind the Science paywall (HTTP 403), Europe PMC has no full text or supplementary files, and no GEO, SRA, BioProject or Dryad record links to PubMed ID 42658938. So the genotypes, pollen-fertility and seed-set phenotypes, and any sequencing data cannot be obtained without a subscription.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (also, on the paper text). No candidate label table is accessible. Any plausible target — pollen or spikelet fertility per plant, or 'this locus is a gamete killer' per genome — would have to be built by hand from figure panels or from a paywalled supplement, i.e. constructed rather than read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partly true but moot: the input side (Oryza genome assemblies for the AA-genome species) is public in NCBI/Ensembl Plants and the repo's BLAST/exonerate scripts show how the locus is located. The inputs exist; the labels do not.

a4_units_stated.note: Cannot check. No table was retrievable, so no units column was seen. Fertility percentages and transmission ratios are quoted in the paper's figures only.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on the biology regardless of access. This is a one-locus mechanism study: the world's catalogue of characterised rice hybrid-sterility toxin-antidote loci is on the order of ten to twenty (S5, Sa, qHMS7, S1, RHS3 ...), far under the ~400-row floor for classification. Mapping-population phenotypes would be hundreds of plants but for a single segregating cross.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Oryza AA-genome assemblies, roughly 0.4 GB per genome, about 5 GB for a dozen; the code archive is 17 KB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot check: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cannot trace. The gamete-abortion phenotype is a real microscope/field measurement, which would be fine, but with no accessible table there is nothing to trace it in. For a sequence-based 'is this ORF a gamete-killer toxin' task the labels would come from a handful of published papers, i.e. literature curation, not a uniform assay.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: n/a — with no label table there is nothing to join.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: there is no accessible labelled data from this paper to train or test anything on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use rice genome sequence around a locus to predict whether it kills the gametes of hybrid plants.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model the DNA and protein sequence of a candidate locus from each Oryza (rice) genome. Number of labelled examples: unknown, but almost certainly fewer than fifty characterised loci exist worldwide.
plain_idea.predict: Whether that locus acts as a selfish toxin-antidote element that aborts gametes in a hybrid. The true answer comes from counting dead pollen grains and unfilled seeds in crossing experiments, which is slow glasshouse and microscope work reported one locus per paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Rice breeders trying to cross Asian and African rice for higher yield would want a list of which genome regions to avoid or edit; even a failed model would say how much of gamete-killing behaviour is readable from sequence.

ml_idea: Considered and dropped: predict from Oryza genome sequence whether a locus behaves as a gamete-killing toxin-antidote element (and, within a cross, predict pollen fertility from genotype). Dropped because the paper releases no data — the only public artifact is a 17 KB code archive — and because the global number of characterised hybrid-sterility loci is roughly an order of magnitude too small for supervised learning.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: evaluation stopped at the first Part A killer, so no feature table was designed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the files in the Zenodo deposit (one call, 17 KB zip, zero data files) and run NCBI elink from the PubMed ID (zero repository links). Both done; both negative.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: no data is downloadable. The only public artifact is a 16.8 KB code-only Zenodo/GitHub deposit whose README says 'This repository contains code only'; the supplement is paywalled (HTTP 403) and there are no GEO, SRA, BioProject or Dryad records linked to the paper. A5 would fail too even with access, because this is a single-locus molecular mechanism study and only a handful of rice hybrid-sterility loci are characterised worldwide. Genuinely interesting biology, not a machine-learning dataset.
